body.statement: Using the feasible-frame handle \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{fix}}\), determine the exact value of \(\rho_k(K,R)\) for each fixed \(k\ge2\), where the infimum ranges over every \(p,m,M,s,V\) satisfying \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), \(M/m=K\), and \(V/s=R\), and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\). In particular, establish whether every such Gaussian objective satisfies \(\gamma_k(F)\ge k/[1+(k-1)KR]\), or construct a member of this class violating the inequality and derive the corrected fixed-budget frontier.
body.justification: The dimension-free frontier is closed, but exact finite-budget geometry may yield a materially stronger certificate for the small budgets used in practice.
body.gap: The constructed family attains the rational expression in the vanishing-contrast limit, while neither generic weak-submodularity theory nor the current angular comparison proves it is universal.
body.consumer: A fixed-budget trial planner would replace the asymptotic dimension-free certificate by the best possible finite-\(k\) guarantee.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether every admissible Gaussian objective at one fixed \(k\geq2\) satisfies \(\gamma_k(F)\geq k/[1+(k-1)KR]\), or whether a feasible residual-score frame violates that inequality.
obligation.obstruction: The universal proof separately lower-bounds the coordinate chordal losses and upper-bounds the joint chordal loss.  Those two inequalities are jointly sharp only in a growing-budget limit; the frozen assumptions do not force their equality conditions to align at a fixed finite budget.
obligation.attempted: The exact singleton-to-joint ratio was reduced to the normalized Schur-complement frame and hemisphere scores.  The radial unequal-scale family attains the proposed rational expression in a vanishing-contrast limit, but optimizing over all feasible nonradial frames and score pairs was not closed without replacing the exact angular losses by the global Lipschitz envelope, which returns only \(1/(KR)\).
obligation.partial_result:
The proved universal inequality gives
\[
 \rho_k(K,R)\geq\frac1{KR},
\]
while the legal unequal-scale construction gives, for every fixed \(k\geq2\),
\[
 \rho_k(K,R)\leq\frac{k}{1+(k-1)KR}.
\]
The two bounds coincide as \(k\to\infty\), establishing the exact dimension-free frontier.  Equality at fixed finite \(k\) remains unresolved.
